SUAS-010 — System Specification Registry & Cross-Reference

The SuperUnicode meta-standard: an embedded, binary-encoded dependency registry that makes the specification tree a machine-verifiable artefact of the kernel image (a UAX #41 analog).

SUAS-010 (SSRE) is the tenth SuperUnicode Architecture Standard and the meta-standard of the set — the normative registry and deterministic linkage protocol that governs how every SUAS standard, SUTS data specification, and SUTR architecture report cross-references one another inside the OpenWindows microkernel. It is the one architecture standard that governs the other architecture standards.

UAX #41 is the Unicode Consortium’s attempt to answer a question no other Unicode technical report asks: which specifications depend on which? Its answer is a bibliography — a human-readable table of contents, maintained by hand, read by humans, and enforced by nothing. SSRE keeps the question and replaces the answer with an embedded binary registry, so that version mismatches, missing prerequisite SUTS modules, and invalid architectural dependencies are caught instantly, at compile time, before an image is produced.

Dual-layer architecture

Layer Role
SUCD — offline reference Human-readable specification manifests and normative reference lists, for documentation, external compilers, and compliance tooling
SSRE — runtime kernel Immutable, byte-packed binary tables (ssre_spec_record_t) embedded in the kernel image and queried in O(1)

As with SIP and SCSS, the seeding brief named the offline layer “SUCA”; in this corpus SUCA is already the SuperUnicode Collation Algorithm (SUTS-001), so SSRE names SUCD as its reference layer.

The cross-reference kinds

Where a UAX #41 bibliography records only that one document references another, SSRE classifies what kind of thing is being referenced — and this is the distinction that makes the registry enforceable rather than merely informative.

Kind Family Meaning
SUAS_SSRE_KIND_MANDATORY SUAS A non-negotiable architectural invariant
SUAS_SSRE_KIND_OPTIONAL SUTS An optional data specification
SUAS_SSRE_KIND_REFERENCE SUTR An architecture report

A dependency asserting is_mandatory is satisfiable only against a MANDATORY specification. An application that declares a mandatory dependency on an optional SUTS data specification has made an architectural error, and SSRE rejects it rather than quietly accommodating it.

The dependency descriptor

typedef struct {
const char *spec_id; /* e.g. "SUTS-003", "SUAS-009" */
uint8_t min_version_major;
uint8_t min_version_minor;
bool is_mandatory; /* true if SUAS, false if optional SUTS */
} ssre_dependency_descriptor_t;

Two enforcement surfaces

Surface Question it answers Provider known Failure
SUAS_SSRE_REQUIRE_DEP Does the header I am compiling against match? At build time Compilation halts
suas_ssre_verify_dependency Does the image I am loading actually contain it? At load time Module load rejected

Every operator in SUAS_SSRE_VALIDATE_DEP is a preprocessor operator, so the predicate is valid inside #if — which is what makes a compile-time gate possible at all. A module whose provider declares its version as integer literals enforces its own prerequisite directly:

#if !SUAS_SSRE_VALIDATE_DEP(1, 0, SUTS_SLDF_VERSION_MAJOR, SUTS_SLDF_VERSION_MINOR)
#error "SSRE: schema misalignment with SUTS-003 (SLDF)"
#endif

SUAS_SSRE_REQUIRE_DEP applies the same predicate through the classic C99 negative-array-bound idiom, with a caller-chosen symbol so several gates may coexist in one translation unit. Both surfaces implement the identical partial order, so they can never disagree.

The curated registry

Kind Count Members
MANDATORY 16 SUAS-001 (SDF) … SUAS-009 (SIP), SUAS-010 (SSRE), SUAS-011 (SCMS), SUAS-012 (SUCD), SUAS-013 (SISR), SUAS-014 (SUVTL), SUAS-015 (SUAMR), SUAS-016 (SUKEMET)
OPTIONAL 9 SUTS-001 (SUCA), SUTS-002 (SRE), SUTS-003 (SLDF), SUTS-004 (SIVD), SUTS-005 (SCSS), SUTS-006 (SIDN), SUTS-007 (SUEPS), SUTS-008 (SUSCH), SUTS-009 (SULDF)
REFERENCE 13 SUTR-0 through SUTR-012

Each record carries the specification identifier, its family acronym, the reference unit implementing it (e.g. suts_sldf), its registered version, its kind, and the SUCM conformance tier it claims. The registry maps specification → unit, and suas_ssre_spec_of_module provides the inverse — the operation a documentation generator needs in order to print, for any engine, the specification that governs it.

Resolution

The registry is a static array of at most SUAS_SSRE_REGISTRY_CAPACITY (64) records, indexed once into a fixed array of SUAS_SSRE_INDEX_SIZE (256) open-addressing slots (FNV-1a hash over the identifier bytes, linear probing). Identifiers are short NUL-terminated ASCII, so hashing and equality are bounded single-pass loops and a freestanding image needs no <string.h> at all.

Operation Cost
suas_ssre_lookup O(1) expected (bounded probes), no allocation
suas_ssre_verify_dependency O(1) expected — one lookup plus constant work
suas_ssre_verify_set / _first_missing O(count)
suas_ssre_spec_of_module O(n) over the registry; tooling path, not the boot path
Feature Status
Embedded binary registry in the kernel image Yes
Compile-time gate usable inside #if Yes
Mandatory-implies-MANDATORY rejection Yes
Bidirectional specification ↔ unit cross-reference Yes
Zero allocation, freestanding C99 Yes
Registry self-consistency under test Yes

Numbering note

The SUAS series is contiguous: SUAS-001 through SUAS-013 are all allocated, in authorship order, and no number is reserved or held back. This standard is SUAS-010.

It was first published as SUAS-011, with SUAS-010 left as a deliberate gap, because a skipped number in a small series reads as a transcription error rather than as a decision — so both it and SCMS were shifted down by one. Citations predating that shift that say SUAS-011 (SSRE) mean this standard; those that say SUAS-012 (SCMS) mean SUAS-011 (SCMS). Those citations are strictly historical: SUAS-012 now names SUCD, and SUAS-013 names SISR.

Reference implementation: include/suas/suas_ssre.h + src/suas/suas_ssre.c (freestanding C99, no heap), registered in suas_static.

Source of truth: docs/suas/SUAS-010-ssre.md in the repository.
